newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian president ends talks on new PM.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian president ends talks on new PM.

text.p: Slovenian President Milan Kucan on Wednesday ended a second round of talks with party leaders aimed at selecting a prime minister, his spokeswoman Spela Furlan said.
The president, who must name a candidate by January 3, will issue a statement on the talks at 0930 GMT on Thursday and analysts predicted he might name the candidate then.
Igor Luksic, professor of politics at Ljubljana University, told Reuters current Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek, 46, was most likely to get the mandate.
Drnovsek's centre-left Liberal Democrats are the strongest party with 25 out of 90 parliamentary seats.

The "Spring" alliance of three rightist parties, which together control 45 seats -- one short of an absolute majority -- has thrown its weight behind conservative People's Party leader Marjan Podobnik, 35.
Parliament must elect a prime minister with an absolute majority in two attempts. If it fails, it can decide by a simple majority. If all three attempts fail, the president can call early elections.
